kind: Recovery-only inventory; no new collation or edition changes
scope: Every one of the 54 original missing report basenames, including each JSON and Markdown file separately. Recoveries of unrelated already-published reports and additional scripts do not count toward these 54.

definitions.original-bytes: Surviving original report bytes, with original byte identity established; none recovered among these 54.
definitions.complete-transcript-replay: Complete report content mechanically recreated from retained historical literal source/generator. No inference of unavailable readings and no original-byte identity claim.
definitions.partial-literal-evidence-source: Exact retained tool input/output, report fragments or related literal audit records survive, but the complete original report is not recovered. For paired Markdown reports, related JSON evidence does not mean original Markdown text survives.
definitions.compacted-summary-only: Substantive scope/findings/corrections survive only in a compacted summary, recovery summary or handoff; not original report bodies.
definitions.no-recoverable-body: Only filename, scope/count metadata or distinct secondary-audit records are located; no substantive original report body is recovered.

cautions: A recovered source script is not automatically a recovered report. Missing input ledgers and dynamic source metadata remain explicit dependencies.
The complete replayed Gcn late report is a record of a failed bounded reading attempt, not successful continuous lexical collation.
Historical findings and superseded locators are preserved as historical evidence. Recovery does not adopt them into the edition or increase confidence.
Original stdout excerpts for root-final-audit and langtang-junction-audit deliberately omitted evidence_sha256, so neither is a complete original JSON recovery.
The 54 basenames are the original audit denominator. New preservation files, repeated copies and provenance documents do not reduce it.
This inventory is tied to the inspected commit; later publication of retained fragments may improve individual evidence descriptions without restoring complete reports.
